findings.title: Assertions (g) and (i) are not failure-specific; their names overstate what they discriminate
findings.evidence: The claim function returns 'verified_predecessor_required' from two independent places: supabase/migrations/20260910104500_engineering_native_ownership.sql:317-321 (any earlier task that is not succeeded+passed) and :333-338. It also passes task(2,31)'s own input admission, whose producer is task(1,31)'s attempt, so :333-337 would deny task(3,31) even if task(2,31) had succeeded. task(3,31) is likewise 'blocked' from creation while task(2,31) is queued, running or failed. So 'third change cannot claim behind a failed predecessor' and 'failed predecessor keeps the third change blocked' would pass unchanged with no failure at all. Mutation 3 only flips the test's expected value, so it exercises the harness, not product code. Assertion (h) (attempt count = 1) is trivially true because no retry is attempted. All of this follows the unit spec, which prescribes these exact calls. (c) and (d) are genuinely discriminating.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional: say in a SQL comment or the PR body that (g), (h) and (i) are state regression guards, as (j) already does, rather than failure-discriminating checks. Otherwise no change is needed for this unit's ACs.

findings.title: With the 560 guard removed, registration hits a pkey collision instead of succeeding
findings.evidence: In my mutation run (fixture fa2018e2), not ok 116 was 'caught: 23505: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "native_verifier_registered_objects_pkey"'. The proof reuses the ovd561-synthetic/result storage object that task(1,31) already registered. The spec's failure_first text said registration 'now succeeds'. The PR body describes this accurately ('reaches the insert'). The assertion still pins errcode and message exactly, so it remains non-vacuous.
findings.suggested_fix: None required. A future tightening could use a fresh storage object, so the mutation would show an actual successful registration.
